# Knife skills

Good cuts come from deliberate repetition. I practise one cut at a time, slowly, with a pile of onions: dice, julienne, brunoise. The aim is uniform pieces, which cook evenly, and the speed arrives later on its own. When a movement goes wrong I isolate it, slow it down further and repeat it until the muscle memory takes over.

A sharp blade is safer than a dull one. A curled-finger claw grip protects the knuckles, and the guiding thumb stays behind the fingertips. I keep the knives on a magnetic strip and hone them before every session; see [[Sharpening stones]] for the monthly routine.

Fifteen minutes a day beats a long session once a week.
